question_text: Which of the following correctly describes distribution?

options.A: DDT achieves high concentrations in fat but is not toxic to adipose tissue

explanation: DDT achieves high concentrations in fat but is not toxic to adipose tissue. Tissue of highest concentration is not necessarily the target organ

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes distribution?

options.A: Plasma proteins (especially albumin) serve as storage depot for acidic drugs and toxicants

explanation: Plasma proteins (especially albumin) serve as storage depot for acidic drugs and toxicants. Only unbound chemical is available for distribution and effects

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes distribution?

options.B: The blood-brain barrier limits entry of polar and large molecules into the CNS

explanation: The blood-brain barrier limits entry of polar and large molecules into the CNS. Tight junctions and P-gp efflux maintain the barrier

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes distribution?

options.A: Lipophilic chemicals can cross the placenta; P-gp provides protection by efflux back to maternal circulation

explanation: Lipophilic chemicals can cross the placenta; P-gp provides protection by efflux back to maternal circulation. Fetus is particularly vulnerable due to immature detoxification

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes excretion?

options.D: Urinary excretion involves glomerular filtration, active tubular secretion, and passive tubular reabsorption

explanation: Urinary excretion involves glomerular filtration, active tubular secretion, and passive tubular reabsorption. Molecules <60 kDa pass through glomerular pores; ionized forms are reabsorbed less

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes excretion?

options.A: Enterohepatic circulation involves biliary excretion followed by reabsorption from intestine

explanation: Enterohepatic circulation involves biliary excretion followed by reabsorption from intestine. Bacterial glucuronidases hydrolyze conjugates, releasing parent compound

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes excretion?

options.C: Breast milk serves as a route of elimination for lipophilic xenobiotics

explanation: Breast milk serves as a route of elimination for lipophilic xenobiotics. This is also a route of infant exposure

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes excretion?

options.B: Fecal excretion includes nonabsorbed ingesta, biliary excretion, and direct intestinal secretion

explanation: Fecal excretion includes nonabsorbed ingesta, biliary excretion, and direct intestinal secretion. MRP2 and BCRP actively secrete compounds into intestinal lumen

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.D: Toxicokinetics is the quantitative study of ADME through measurement of concentrations in biological matrices vs time

explanation: Toxicokinetics is the quantitative study of ADME through measurement of concentrations in biological matrices vs time. Derived from pharmacokinetics studies with drugs

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cmax and AUC are the two most common dose metrics in toxicokinetic studies
options.D: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Cmax and AUC are the two most common dose metrics in toxicokinetic studies. Cmax is peak concentration; AUC is area under concentration-time curve

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.B: The trapezoidal method calculates AUC by summing areas of trapezoids from the concentration-time curve
options.C: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: The trapezoidal method calculates AUC by summing areas of trapezoids from the concentration-time curve. AUC0-inf adds Clast/Kel for terminal area

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Mean residence time (MRT) = AUMC/AUC. AUMC is area under first moment curve (concentration x time)

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.D: At least 2 early and 3 terminal elimination phase time points needed for TK studies

explanation: At least 2 early and 3 terminal elimination phase time points needed for TK studies. Samples should show concentration changes by factor of 2 or order of magnitude

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.B: No more than 10% of blood volume should be drawn during AUC sampling interval

explanation: No more than 10% of blood volume should be drawn during AUC sampling interval. Prevents compromising physiological status

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: One-compartment model assumes body as single homogeneous compartment with instantaneous distribution

explanation: One-compartment model assumes body as single homogeneous compartment with instantaneous distribution. Appropriate for rapidly distributing compounds

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: PBTK models incorporate actual anatomical and physiological parameters (tissue volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients)
options.D: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: PBTK models incorporate actual anatomical and physiological parameters (tissue volumes, blood flows, partition coefficients). Allows mechanistic prediction of tissue concentrations

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.C: Clearance is the volume of blood completely cleared of chemical per unit time

explanation: Clearance is the volume of blood completely cleared of chemical per unit time. Hepatic clearance depends on intrinsic clearance, blood flow, and protein binding

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: Cannot be used for risk assessment
options.D: Elimination half-life: t1/2 = 0.693/ke for first-order elimination

explanation: Elimination half-life: t1/2 = 0.693/ke for first-order elimination. Half-life doubles when clearance decreases by half

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.C: Bioavailability F = AUC_oral / (AUC_IV x dose_oral/dose_IV) x 100%

explanation: Bioavailability F = AUC_oral / (AUC_IV x dose_oral/dose_IV) x 100%. F < 100% indicates incomplete absorption or first-pass metabolism

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes toxicokinetics?

options.A: Nonlinear kinetics occur when elimination processes become saturated at high doses
options.B: Cannot be used for risk assessment

explanation: Nonlinear kinetics occur when elimination processes become saturated at high doses. AUC increases disproportionately; half-life may increase

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes air pollution?

options.B: PM2.5 is more harmful than PM10 because smaller particles penetrate deeper into alveoli
options.D: No health effects at ambient levels

explanation: PM2.5 is more harmful than PM10 because smaller particles penetrate deeper into alveoli. PM10 is largely deposited in upper airways

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes air pollution?

options.B: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions of NOx and VOCs
options.D: No health effects at ambient levels

explanation: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions of NOx and VOCs. Causes respiratory inflammation and decreased lung function

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes air pollution?

options.B: EPA NAAQS set limits for criteria pollutants including PM2.5, PM10, O3, CO, SO2, NO2, and lead

explanation: EPA NAAQS set limits for criteria pollutants including PM2.5, PM10, O3, CO, SO2, NO2, and lead. NAAQS are set to protect public health with adequate margin of safety

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes analytical tox?

options.B: GC-MS is the gold standard for volatile and semi-volatile compound identification in forensic toxicology

explanation: GC-MS is the gold standard for volatile and semi-volatile compound identification in forensic toxicology. Provides chromatographic separation and mass spectral identification

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes analytical tox?

options.A: LC-MS/MS has replaced immunoassay for confirmatory drug testing due to higher specificity

explanation: LC-MS/MS has replaced immunoassay for confirmatory drug testing due to higher specificity. MRM provides excellent selectivity and sensitivity

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes analytical tox?

options.B: Immunoassays are used for initial screening but can produce false positives due to cross-reactivity

explanation: Immunoassays are used for initial screening but can produce false positives due to cross-reactivity. Confirmation by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS is required

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes clinical tox?

options.C: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is the antidote for acetaminophen toxicity, replenishing glutathione

explanation: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is the antidote for acetaminophen toxicity, replenishing glutathione. Most effective within 8-10 hours of ingestion

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes clinical tox?

options.A: Atropine blocks muscarinic effects in organophosphate poisoning but does not reverse nicotinic effects

explanation: Atropine blocks muscarinic effects in organophosphate poisoning but does not reverse nicotinic effects. Pralidoxime is needed for AChE reactivation

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding occupational tox EXCEPT:

options.D: TLV-TWA is the 8-hour time-weighted average; TLV-STEL is 15-minute; TLV-C is ceiling

explanation: TLV-TWA is the 8-hour time-weighted average; TLV-STEL is 15-minute; TLV-C is ceiling. TLVs are guidelines, not legally enforceable (unlike OSHA PELs)

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding occupational tox EXCEPT:

options.B: Biological Exposure Indices (BEIs) complement air monitoring by reflecting total exposure via all routes

explanation: Biological Exposure Indices (BEIs) complement air monitoring by reflecting total exposure via all routes. BEIs are guidelines for levels in biological specimens

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding regulatory tox EXCEPT:

options.B: TSCA regulates chemical substances in commerce through EPA pre-manufacture notification
options.C: FIFRA does not require efficacy data

explanation: TSCA regulates chemical substances in commerce through EPA pre-manufacture notification. EPA can require testing and restrict new chemicals

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding regulatory tox EXCEPT:

options.A: FIFRA requires EPA registration of all pesticides with mammalian toxicity, environmental fate, and efficacy data
options.B: FIFRA does not require efficacy data

explanation: FIFRA requires EPA registration of all pesticides with mammalian toxicity, environmental fate, and efficacy data. Registration must be renewed periodically

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding study design EXCEPT:

options.A: Subchronic studies are 90-day rodent and 6-month non-rodent studies to identify target organs

explanation: Subchronic studies are 90-day rodent and 6-month non-rodent studies to identify target organs. Used to establish dose ranges for chronic studies

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding study design EXCEPT:

options.B: Satellite groups always sacrificed at interim
options.D: Chronic rodent studies are typically 2 years (lifetime) to detect carcinogenic potential

explanation: Chronic rodent studies are typically 2 years (lifetime) to detect carcinogenic potential. Minimum 50 animals/sex/group for carcinogenicity studies

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding study design EXCEPT:

options.B: Satellite groups provide interim sacrifices or recovery assessments in toxicity studies

explanation: Satellite groups provide interim sacrifices or recovery assessments in toxicity studies. Recovery groups assess reversibility of treatment effects

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding study design EXCEPT:

options.B: The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is the highest dose that does not shorten survival by >10%

explanation: The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is the highest dose that does not shorten survival by >10%. Used as high dose in carcinogenicity bioassays

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes carcinogenicity?

options.A: The 2-year rodent bioassay is the gold standard for carcinogenicity assessment

explanation: The 2-year rodent bioassay is the gold standard for carcinogenicity assessment. Uses rats and mice at 3 dose levels plus controls

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes carcinogenicity?

options.C: The polyk adjustment accounts for differential mortality in carcinogenicity bioassays
options.D: Tumor incidence not adjusted for mortality

explanation: The polyk adjustment accounts for differential mortality in carcinogenicity bioassays. Adjusts tumor incidence for animals that died early

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes carcinogenicity?

options.A: Peto analysis is the preferred statistical method for evaluating tumor incidence
options.C: Tumor incidence not adjusted for mortality

explanation: Peto analysis is the preferred statistical method for evaluating tumor incidence. Accounts for competing risks of non-tumor death
